label: late original-phase j, mainly right after r (very sparse)
explanation: Extremely sparse feature (350 activations in 1M sequences). About 88% of activation mass is on input j during the original phase at positions 4-7 (positions 0-3 never fire). Rate is highest when the previous input is r (about 65% of mass; all of the top examples are ... r j), then i. Sequences starting with t are overrepresented, which suggests a further dependence on the prefix. It never fires in the copy phase. A small amount fires on <DEL> or on other tokens after r r. Precision is very low: only about 0.4% of late-position j inputs activate it, and only about 2% of r-then-j inputs do, so the real trigger is a narrow prefix conjunction that no simple predicate captures. The predicate names the dominant context; it does not explain which sequences fire.
